title: Fork and Configure Upstream Remote
description: Fork a public practice repository on GitHub, clone your fork to your computer, and set up the original repo as an `upstream` remote.
steps: Go to a public practice repository on GitHub (or use: https://github.com/octocat/Spoon-Knife)
Click the 'Fork' button in the top right corner of the page
Create the fork under your personal GitHub account
On YOUR newly created fork page, copy the HTTPS clone URL
In your terminal, clone your fork: `git clone <YOUR_FORK_URL> spoon-knife-fork`
Check configured remotes: `git remote -v` — notice `origin` points to YOUR fork
Now add the original project as `upstream`: `git remote add upstream https://github.com/octocat/Spoon-Knife.git`
Verify again: `git remote -v` — you should now see 4 lines: 2 for `origin` (your fork) and 2 for `upstream` (original repo)!
expected_output: `git remote -v` lists both `origin` (your personal fork) and `upstream` (original author's repo).
tips: A fork is a server-side copy on GitHub; a clone is a local copy on your hard drive.
`upstream` is the standard convention name for the original repository you forked from.
